questions.question: Name the four flows between businesses and government in the circular flow and give one example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Businesses to government: goods and services (real), e.g. textbooks, medicines, construction; taxes (money), e.g. company income tax, VAT paid over, PAYE paid over. Government to businesses: payment for goods and services and subsidies (money), e.g. paying the builder for classrooms, manufacturing incentives; public goods, infrastructure and services (real), e.g. roads, ports, electricity, water, courts, company registration.

questions.question: Explain how government acts as a consumer and as a producer in relation to businesses. Refer to all three spheres and explain why tenders are required.
questions.expected_answer: Consumer: government buys goods and services from businesses (public procurement), e.g. national — police vehicles, defence equipment, national road contracts; provincial — textbooks, school furniture, medicines, school and clinic buildings; local — pipes, refuse trucks, road building. Producer: government supplies infrastructure and services, e.g. national — national roads, ports, rail, the power grid, CIPC, SARS customs, courts; provincial — provincial roads, educated and healthy workers; local — water, electricity distribution, refuse removal, zoning. Section 217 of the Constitution requires procurement to be fair, equitable, transparent, competitive and cost-effective, so larger contracts go out to tender to give businesses an equal chance and get value for money.

questions.question: A business buys materials for R10 000 plus VAT and sells its product for R20 000 plus VAT. Calculate the input tax, output tax and the amount paid to SARS at 15%. Name two other taxes or deductions a business pays over to SARS.
questions.expected_answer: Input tax = 15% of R10 000 = R1 500. Output tax = 15% of R20 000 = R3 000. Paid to SARS = R3 000 − R1 500 = R1 500. Other taxes: company income tax at 27% of taxable income; PAYE deducted from employees' salaries; also UIF contributions and customs or excise duties where relevant.
